# gpa-calculator-mcp

> GPA calculator MCP server for AI apps. Calculate GPA, CGPA, SGPA, weighted GPA, weighted grades, a target GPA, grades on the final and letter grade conversion. Works offline, no account. Free and open source, works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and others.

## Setup
- Run with npx -y gpa-calculator-mcp
- Works offline, no account. No environment variables, no network calls and no data is stored.
- All seven tools are read only. They only do arithmetic on the numbers you pass in.

## How it compares

| Option | Needs login or school access | Runs offline | Focus | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPA Calculator MCP (this server) | No | Yes | Just the numbers. GPA, CGPA, SGPA, weighted grades, targets and conversions. | You have numbers or want to plan and just need the calculation. |
| LMS MCP servers (like Brightspace, Canvas, Moodle, Google Classroom) | Often yes, connects to a school system | Usually no | Pulls grades, due dates and course data from a learning system. Some include a target grade calculator. | You want to pull data straight from your courses, not type numbers in. |

For a student who just wants the number, a focused offline calculator avoids signing in, avoids connecting to a school server and keeps the task to arithmetic. If you already pull grades from an LMS, you can still pass those numbers to this calculator.

## Grade conversion tables
The server has six grade scales that are built in. The scale parameter takes one of the six ids below, and any other value is rejected before the tool runs. Run list_scales to print the same tables.

### us4 (US 4.0 scale)
- A: 93 to 100, 4.0 grade points
- A-: 90 to 92, 3.7 grade points
- B+: 87 to 89, 3.3 grade points
- B: 83 to 86, 3.0 grade points
- B-: 80 to 82, 2.7 grade points
- C+: 77 to 79, 2.3 grade points
- C: 73 to 76, 2.0 grade points
- C-: 70 to 72, 1.7 grade points
- D+: 67 to 69, 1.3 grade points
- D: 63 to 66, 1.0 grade points
- D-: 60 to 62, 0.7 grade points
- F: 0 to 59, 0.0 grade points

### us4plus (US 4.3 scale, A+ is 4.3)
- A+: 97 to 100, 4.3 grade points
- A: 93 to 96, 4.0 grade points
- A-: 90 to 92, 3.7 grade points
- B+: 87 to 89, 3.3 grade points
- B: 83 to 86, 3.0 grade points
- B-: 80 to 82, 2.7 grade points
- C+: 77 to 79, 2.3 grade points
- C: 73 to 76, 2.0 grade points
- C-: 70 to 72, 1.7 grade points
- D+: 67 to 69, 1.3 grade points
- D: 63 to 66, 1.0 grade points
- D-: 60 to 62, 0.7 grade points
- F: 0 to 59, 0.0 grade points

### ontario-college (Ontario college 4.0 scale, common version, check your school's table)
- A+: 90 to 100, 4.0 grade points
- A: 80 to 89, 4.0 grade points
- B+: 75 to 79, 3.5 grade points
- B: 70 to 74, 3.0 grade points
- C+: 65 to 69, 2.5 grade points
- C: 60 to 64, 2.0 grade points
- D: 50 to 59, 1.0 grade points
- F: 0 to 49, 0.0 grade points

### uk-classification (UK degree classification, standard boundaries, check your school's table)
- 1st: 70 to 100, 4.0 grade points
- 2:1: 60 to 69, 3.3 grade points
- 2:2: 50 to 59, 2.7 grade points
- 3rd: 40 to 49, 2.0 grade points
- F: 0 to 39, 0.0 grade points

The grade points are a plain mapping from the class to a number, so that the GPA tools can add up classified work. UK universities do not usually give a classification grade points. A first maps to 4.0, a 2:1 to 3.3, a 2:2 to 2.7 and a third to 2.0. Ask in a letter as "1st", "2:1", "2:2" or "3rd", or pass a percentage and the server picks the class.

### australia-hd (Australian 7.0 scale, HD is 7, common version, check your school's table)
- HD: 80 to 100, 7.0 grade points
- D: 70 to 79, 6.0 grade points
- C: 60 to 69, 5.0 grade points
- P: 50 to 59, 4.0 grade points
- F: 0 to 49, 0.0 grade points

### weighted-5.0 (US weighted 5.0 scale, A is 5.0, one point above us4, check your school's table)
- A: 93 to 100, 5.0 grade points
- A-: 90 to 92, 4.7 grade points
- B+: 87 to 89, 4.3 grade points
- B: 83 to 86, 4.0 grade points
- B-: 80 to 82, 3.7 grade points
- C+: 77 to 79, 3.3 grade points
- C: 73 to 76, 3.0 grade points
- C-: 70 to 72, 2.7 grade points
- D+: 67 to 69, 2.3 grade points
- D: 63 to 66, 2.0 grade points
- D-: 60 to 62, 1.7 grade points
- F: 0 to 59, 0.0 grade points

The weighted-5.0 table is a plain mapping rather than one school's official table: it keeps the us4 percentage cutoffs and puts every letter above F one point higher, so an A is 5.0 and an A- is 4.7. It works when your school reports a weighted GPA on a 5.0 top. Pass the scale id "weighted-5.0" wherever a tool takes a scale, for example "What's my weighted GPA on a 5.0 scale?"

## Tools

Every tool below has its parameters and one example call. An example call is JSON in the MCP tools/call shape: the tool name plus its arguments. All seven tools are read only.

Every tool also has an output schema and returns the numbers as fields next to the text, so a client that reads JSON gets the numbers without taking them out of the sentence. The Structured output line under each tool names the fields.

### calculate_gpa
Calculate a GPA from a list of courses with credits and grades, optionally weighted with a credit multiplier on each course, and optionally combined with an earlier GPA and credit total. The GPA for the courses you pass is the term GPA, and adding earlier work with prior_gpa and prior_credits gives the cumulative GPA. Inputs: courses (each with credits greater than 0, a grade that is a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87, and an optional credit_multiplier greater than 0 such as 1.1 for an AP class), a scale id, and optional prior_gpa and prior_credits to fold in earlier terms. A credit_multiplier above 1 gives a course more weight in the weighted GPA, and when any course has one other than 1 the tool also returns weighted_gpa and weighted_credits. The term GPA still uses the plain credits. Pass prior_gpa and prior_credits together, or leave both out. Passing only one of the two is an error, so the tool says which one is missing. Example prompt: "What's my GPA if I got an A in 3 credits, a B+ in 4 credits and a C in 3 credits?"

Parameters:
- courses (array, required): The courses to include. Each needs credits (greater than 0) and a grade (a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87). name is optional, and so is credit_multiplier (greater than 0), which gives a course more weight in the weighted GPA.
  - name (string, optional): Course name.
  - credits (number, required): Credits for the course, must be greater than 0.
  - grade (string or number, required): A letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%".
  - credit_multiplier (number, optional): Optional multiplier on the credits for a weighted GPA, greater than 0, like 1.1 for an AP class. Defaults to 1.
- scale (string enum, optional, default "us4"): Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.
- prior_gpa (number, optional): GPA from earlier terms, 0 to 7. Pass this together with prior_credits to get a cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error.
- prior_credits (number, optional): Credits from earlier terms, 0 or more. Pass this together with prior_gpa to get a cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error.

Example call: `{"name":"calculate_gpa","arguments":{"courses":[{"name":"Calculus","credits":3,"grade":"A"},{"name":"Physics","credits":4,"grade":"B+"},{"name":"History","credits":3,"grade":"C"}],"scale":"us4"}}`

Output: one line per course ("Calculus: A, 4.0 points x 3 credits"), then "GPA for these courses: 3.12 across 10 credits (US 4.0 scale)." With a credit multiplier on a course, the line adds the multiplier and the answer adds the weighted GPA and weighted credits. Pass prior_gpa and prior_credits together to also get the cumulative GPA. Passing only one of the two is an error and says which one is missing.

Structured output: scale, scale_name, courses, credits, term_gpa, weighted_gpa and weighted_credits when a credit multiplier other than 1 is passed, and cumulative_gpa and cumulative_credits when the earlier work is folded in. The courses array holds one entry per course with name, credits, letter, points and quality_points, plus credit_multiplier, weighted_credits and weighted_quality_points when the course has a multiplier other than 1.

### convert_grade
Convert a letter or percentage into the matching letter, percentage range and grade points on a grade scale. Inputs: grade (a letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%") and a scale id. Example prompt: "Convert 78 percent to a letter grade on the Ontario college scale."

Parameters:
- grade (string or number, required): A letter like "B+" or a percentage like 87 or "87%".
- scale (string enum, optional, default "us4"): Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

Example call: `{"name":"convert_grade","arguments":{"grade":78,"scale":"ontario-college"}}`

Output: "78 is B+ on the Ontario college 4.0 scale (common version, check your school's table). That letter covers 75 to 79 percent and is worth 3.5 grade points."

Structured output: scale, scale_name, letter, min_percent, max_percent and points.

### needed_on_final
Calculate the score needed on a final exam or last assignment to reach a target course grade. Inputs: current_percent (the average on all the other work, 0 to 100), final_weight_percent (how much the final is worth, greater than 0 and at most 100) and a target. Give the target as target_percent (the course grade you want, 0 to 100), as target_letter (a letter like "B+" or a class like "2:1", whose cutoff comes from the scale table), or as both. The scale id sets the table the letter cutoff comes from. Says so when the target is already locked in or out of reach. Example prompt: "My grade is 85% and the final is worth 40% of the course. What do I need on the final to finish with a B+?"

Parameters:
- current_percent (number, required): Current grade on the work already done, as a percentage between 0 and 100.
- final_weight_percent (number, required): How much the final is worth, greater than 0 and at most 100, as a percentage of the whole course.
- target_percent (number, optional): The course grade you want to finish with, as a percentage between 0 and 100. Leave it out when you pass target_letter.
- target_letter (string, optional): The letter grade you want to finish with, like "B+" or "2:1", read from the scale table. Leave it out when you pass target_percent.
- scale (string enum, optional, default "us4"): Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

Example call: `{"name":"needed_on_final","arguments":{"current_percent":85,"final_weight_percent":40,"target_letter":"B+","scale":"us4"}}`

Output: "You need 90% on the final (worth 40%) to finish with the grade B+, which starts at 87% on the US 4.0 scale. You have 85% on the rest of the course." Give target_percent 80 instead of a letter and the tool says you need 72.5% on the final to finish with 80%.

Structured output: scale, scale_name, current_percent, final_weight_percent, target_percent, needed_percent, possible and already_there, plus target_letter and letter_min_percent when a letter target was given.

### weighted_grade
Combine weighted course parts into the grade so far, plus the worst and best possible finish. Inputs: parts (each with a name, a weight that is a percentage of the whole course greater than 0, and an optional score between 0 and 100; leave the score out for parts that are not marked yet). A weight is a percentage of the whole course, so the parts are never rescaled. Parts that add up to less than 100 leave the rest of the course still to come, and weights that add up to more than 100 are an error. Example prompt: "My course is 20% quizzes, 30% labs, 50% exam. I have 85 on quizzes and 70 on labs. What's my grade so far and what's the best I can finish with?"

Parameters:
- parts (array, required): The weighted parts of the course. Each needs a name and a weight (a percentage of the whole course greater than 0); score is 0 to 100, or leave it out for parts that are not marked yet. Weights are percentages of the whole course, so parts that add up to less than 100 leave the rest of the course still to come.
  - name (string, required): Name of the course part.
  - weight (number, required): Weight as a percentage of the whole course, greater than 0.
  - score (number or null, optional): Score between 0 and 100 for marked parts, or leave out for unmarked parts.

Example call: `{"name":"weighted_grade","arguments":{"parts":[{"name":"Quizzes","weight":20,"score":85},{"name":"Labs","weight":30,"score":70},{"name":"Exam","weight":50}]}}`

Output: one line per part ("Quizzes: weight 20%, 85%"), then "Grade so far: 76% on the 50% of the course that is marked. That banks 38 of the 100 points the course is worth.", then the worst and best possible finish (38% and 88%) and how much of the course is still to come.

Structured output: parts, total_weight, done_weight, remaining_weight, current_grade, earned_points, worst_finish and best_finish. The parts array holds one entry per part with name, weight and score.

### target_gpa_planner
Plan the GPA needed on upcoming credits to reach a target cumulative GPA. Inputs: current_gpa (0 to 7), credits_completed (0 or more), target_gpa (0 to 7), upcoming_credits (greater than 0) and a scale id, which sets the top grade point the scale allows. Says so when the target is already reached or would take more than one term. Example prompt: "I have a 3.1 GPA over 60 credits. What GPA do I need next semester to reach 3.4?"

Parameters:
- current_gpa (number, required): Your cumulative GPA so far, between 0 and 7.
- credits_completed (number, required): Credits already completed, 0 or more.
- target_gpa (number, required): The cumulative GPA you want to reach, between 0 and 7.
- upcoming_credits (number, required): Credits you will take next, greater than 0.
- scale (string enum, optional, default "us4"): Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

Example call: `{"name":"target_gpa_planner","arguments":{"current_gpa":3.1,"credits_completed":60,"target_gpa":3.4,"upcoming_credits":15,"scale":"us4"}}`

Output: "You would need 4.6 on the next 15 credits, but the top of this scale is 4.0. Reaching 3.4 would take more than one term." Ask for 3.2 instead of 3.4 and the same call needs a 3.60 GPA.

Structured output: scale, scale_name, current_gpa, credits_completed, target_gpa, upcoming_credits, needed_gpa, max_points, possible and already_there.

### plan_courses
Plan the grade needed in each upcoming course to reach a target cumulative GPA. Inputs: current_gpa (0 to 7), credits_completed (0 or more), target_gpa (0 to 7), courses (each with an optional name and credits greater than 0) and a scale id, which sets the top grade point the scale allows. It works out the GPA the upcoming credits need, then gives the lowest letter in each course that keeps the plan on track, assuming the other courses meet the same target. Says so when the target is already reached or would take more than one term. Example prompt: "I have a 3.4 GPA over 60 credits. What do I need in each of my four classes next semester to reach 3.5?"

Parameters:
- current_gpa (number, required): Your cumulative GPA so far, between 0 and 7.
- credits_completed (number, required): Credits already completed, 0 or more.
- target_gpa (number, required): The cumulative GPA you want to reach, between 0 and 7.
- courses (array, required): The upcoming courses to plan for. Each needs credits greater than 0, and name is optional.
  - name (string, optional): Course name.
  - credits (number, required): Credits for the course, must be greater than 0.
- scale (string enum, optional, default "us4"): Grade scale id: "us4", "us4plus", "ontario-college", "uk-classification", "australia-hd" or "weighted-5.0". Defaults to "us4". Ask the student which one their school uses if unsure.

Example call: `{"name":"plan_courses","arguments":{"current_gpa":3.4,"credits_completed":60,"target_gpa":3.5,"courses":[{"name":"Calculus","credits":3},{"name":"Physics","credits":3},{"name":"History","credits":3},{"name":"Spanish","credits":3}],"scale":"us4"}}`

Output: "You need a 4.00 GPA over the next 12 credits to reach a cumulative 3.5 (from 3.4 over 60 credits). If every course meets or beats its target below, you reach it." Then one line per course, such as "Calculus: A or better (93% and up, 4.0 points)". When the target is already reached, every course can be any grade that keeps the average at or above it. When the needed GPA is above the top of the scale, each line says that no grade on the scale is enough.

Structured output: scale, scale_name, current_gpa, credits_completed, target_gpa, upcoming_credits, needed_gpa, max_points, possible, already_there and courses. The courses array holds one entry per course with name and credits, plus target_letter, target_min_percent and target_points when the target can be reached.

### list_scales
List the built-in grade scales with their letters, percentage ranges and grade points. Inputs: none. Example prompt: "Show me the grade scales you have built in."

Parameters: none.

Example call: `{"name":"list_scales","arguments":{}}`

Output: the six scales from the tables above, one line per letter with the percentage range and the grade points.

Structured output: scales, an array with one entry per scale. Each entry has id, name and a bands array, and each band has letter, min_percent, max_percent and points.

## FAQ

What is the difference between CGPA and SGPA?

SGPA is the GPA for one term, so the GPA for the courses you pass in. CGPA is the cumulative GPA over every term you have finished. calculate_gpa gives you the term GPA for the courses you pass. Add your earlier GPA and credits as prior_gpa and prior_credits and the tool also gives the cumulative GPA.

Can I include my GPA from last semester?

Yes. Pass your earlier GPA as prior_gpa and your earlier credits as prior_credits to calculate_gpa, along with this term's courses. The tool folds them into a cumulative GPA. Pass both together. Passing only one of the two is an error, so the tool says which one is missing instead of quietly leaving the earlier terms out.

What if my school uses a 4.3 scale?

Use the us4plus scale. It is the us4 scale with A+ worth 4.3. Pass scale "us4plus" to calculate_gpa, convert_grade or target_gpa_planner. Run list_scales to see the full table.

What grade do I need to pass?

It depends on your school and program. On the built in us4 scale, D covers 63 to 66 percent and is usually the lowest passing grade, but many programs require a C or higher. Use needed_on_final to work out what you need on the final, or target_gpa_planner to plan a cumulative GPA. Check your school's handbook for the real cutoff.

Can I ask for a letter grade instead of a percentage?

Yes. Pass target_letter to needed_on_final, for example target_letter "B+", and the tool looks the cutoff up in the scale table. Pass scale "uk-classification" for a UK class such as 2:1. You can pass target_percent as well, and the tool works to the higher of the two.

Do my course parts have to add up to 100?

No. Every weight in weighted_grade is a percentage of the whole course, so you can pass only the parts you know. If you pass 20 percent quizzes and 30 percent labs with scores of 85 and 70, the tool says your grade so far is 76 percent, which banks 38 of the 100 points the course is worth, you finish at 38 percent if you score 0 on everything left, and you finish at 88 percent if you score 100 on everything left. The other 50 percent of the course is still to come. Weights that add up to more than 100 are an error, because a course is graded out of 100.

Can a script read the numbers without reading the sentence?

Yes. Every tool has an output schema and returns the numbers as fields next to the text. A client that reads JSON gets term_gpa, needed_percent and the rest straight away, and a client that only reads the text still gets the same answer as before.
